PullRequest.Title: sessions: bring back pinned canvases after a restart
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes pinned canvases in the Agents window that show *"This canvas is no longer open in its chat"* and never come back when selected, typically after an app restart.

## Root cause

A pin persists only its canvas's identity, and reconnects by finding the same instance ID in its chat's canvas list. Two things can keep the chat from listing it again:

1. **A session that launched without canvases.** A Copilot session decides at launch whether it runs canvases, and nothing changed that decision later. If a session resumed before the client's configuration enabled canvases (for example while the experiment-provided default of `chat.canvases.enabled` had not resolved yet at startup), it ran without canvases until something unrelated relaunched it. Opening its canvases failed with *"Canvases are disabled for this session."*
2. **A canvas the chat no longer has open.** After an Agent Host restart, a lazily activated canvas provider stays dormant until something asks for its canvas, so the chat doesn't list it.

In both cases `PinnedCanvasService` marked the pin unavailable, and selecting it only looked for the canvas again. Nothing asked the chat to open it.

## Fix

**Commit 1 (`sessions`): a shown pin reopens its canvas.** When a pin is shown and its chat's canvas list lacks its canvas, the pin asks the chat to open that instance again through `ISessionsManagementService.openCanvas`, then binds once the chat publishes it.

- Each request is scoped to the session object it was made through. A request through a session that goes away or is replaced is abandoned, its late answer is ignored, and the pin asks again through the returning session.
- After the chat reports the canvas opened, the pin waits up to 10 seconds for that instance, ignoring unrelated membership changes. The host can answer without publishing it, for example when a close superseded the open.
- A failed open marks the pin unavailable and reports why. A declined extension consent (from #348216) shows the standard warning, whose *Try Again* asks again and shows the pin. Showing the pin again retries.
- `openCanvas` now takes only `Pick<ISessionCanvasDefinition, 'canvasId' | 'extensionId'>`, which is all providers use, so a pin can reopen without the chat's canvas definitions, which may not be listed yet after a resume.

**Commit 2 (`agentHost`): a session with stale canvas enablement relaunches.** The runtime refresh compares a session's launch-time canvas enablement with the current configuration.

- A mismatch is a new refresh reason, `canvasesEnabledChanged`, so the session relaunches before its next turn. This also applies when canvases are turned off.
- Opening a canvas relaunches an idle session first. A session with an active turn isn't interrupted: the open reports canvases disabled, and the next turn relaunches it.
- Listing canvases never relaunches a session.
- `isIdleRefreshOperation` treats the `openCanvas` refresh like `startMcpServer`'s: it never sends the chat's draft or takes a turn's cancellation token.
- The setting description now says running sessions pick up changes.

## Recordings

Recorded in Code OSS with a project-scoped demo canvas whose page shows when its provider process started.

**Session resumed with canvases off, then canvases turned on, then the pin is selected.** Before (commit 1 only): the reopen fails with *"Canvases are disabled…"*.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6698978-492c-4586-9e26-f2f5236b45c5

After (both commits): the session relaunches and the canvas is back.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fa4dc1d-d424-4c73-9731-b01a7781d70b

**Lazily activated canvas after a full quit and relaunch.** Before (`main`): the pin goes straight to unavailable.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ece2cc99-d0fb-43bd-828f-2fa5e63d3abd

After: the pin reopens the canvas, and the provider starts at the moment of the click.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14cb72e6-909f-47bb-9f17-6cef289ea358

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files, and `pnpm run precommit` (hygiene) on each commit: passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/browser/pinnedCanvasService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasRegistryService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts`: 656 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: 4484 passing, 17 pending.
- New tests:
  - `pinnedCanvasService.test.ts` covers:
    - a reopen answered before the canvas is published, with unrelated changes in between;
    - no publication in time, then a retry;
    - a session going away and returning;
    - a session replaced before its canvas list loads;
    - a never-loading canvas, with the wait still ending;
    - a failed open with a retry;
    - a declined consent, then *Try Again*.
  - `copilotAgent.test.ts` covers the relaunch sequence:
    - an open during a turn reports canvases disabled, without relaunching;
    - an open while idle relaunches with canvases;
    - turning canvases off relaunches at the next turn.
  - The tests for the changed behavior were checked to fail without the corresponding change.
- End-to-end in Code OSS, as recorded above. After rebasing onto `main`, which brought in the extension-consent changes from #348216, I re-ran the first scenario on this branch: the pin went from unavailable to live in about 2 seconds, and the host logged a refresh with `operation=openCanvas`.

Not covered: canvases that require input. A reopen sends no input, which works when the runtime still has the instance, but this hasn't been tried after a restart.

Scenarios.Scenario: Selecting a persisted pinned canvas whose chat no longer publishes that canvas after restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pin first observes cached/live chat membership. If membership is authoritative and missing, the selection waits for renderer-to-provider openCanvas dispatch, Agent Host chat restoration if cold, optional runtime refresh, and the SDK canvas.open/provider activation before membership can publish and the page can bind. The 10-second publication timer is only a post-open bound and does not add work to the success critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: connection.openSessionCanvas from the workbench/provider into Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per selected missing pin after membership settles, with per-pin in-flight coalescing; explicit later selection retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selection only observed chat membership and marked the pin unavailable when the instance was absent; it did not issue this IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the successful rebind until Agent Host opens and republishes the stable instance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore persisted session/chat state when the target chat is cold
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for the selected request when no resident chat state exists; warm sessions reuse resident state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pinned-canvas selection did not call openSessionCanvas, so it did not put restoration on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restoration must complete before provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK control-plane rpc.canvas.open, potentially activating the canvas extension/provider process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stable-instance RPC for the coalesced reopen; the SDK/runtime handles the same instance identity on retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No SDK canvas-open RPC occurred from selecting an absent pin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete or emit the opened event before membership can become live.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One request per selected missing pin, coalesced by the pin's _reopen state; persisted pins are capped at five. Explicitly selecting again after failure retries, and rapid selection of different pins can leave up to five independent requests in flight.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each pin coalesces its own reopen while in flight or awaiting publication. Agent runtime resolution/restart is serialized by the per-chat queue; the subsequent canvas RPC is not globally limited, but product cardinality is capped at five and ordinary interaction selects pins serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm membership containing the instance binds without an open. Authoritative missing membership triggers one open; successful publication binds and ends observation. Failure/timeout is negatively held as Unavailable until another explicit show. After process restart live canvas membership is intentionally not persisted, so this is a cold path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added reopenCanvas call reaches renderer/Agent Host IPC and SDK canvas.open; guards, cap, and retry lifecycle are explicit in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup duration varies by extension and remote host. The request is user-initiated, capped, coalesced per pin, and replaces a previously nonfunctional path, so the added cost is bounded and required rather than a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff intentionally adds the minimum boundary operation needed to restore a selected stale pin, coalesces it per pin, caps total pin cardinality, and bounds post-open waiting and cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending the next turn, or opening a canvas while idle, after chat canvas enablement changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On every existing turn-refresh path the new in-memory canvas-enable mismatch check can select a restart reason. A mismatch destroys and resumes the SDK session before the turn proceeds. An idle open performs the same refresh before canvas.open; listing canvases explicitly does not refresh. If no mismatch exists, the added check is an in-memory boolean/config lookup after pre-existing refresh work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read stored working-directory/session refresh state as part of the pre-existing refresh check
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per turn refresh, unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stored-directory read and snapshot work already ran for refresh checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already on the turn preparation path before the new mismatch reason is evaluated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Destroy and resume/relaunch the Copilot SDK runtime when canvas enablement mismatches
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per affected live chat per actual configuration transition, deferred until next use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas setting changes did not trigger runtime replacement, so turns continued on the stale launch mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that first turn or idle open so it uses a correctly configured runtime; subsequent operations reuse the replacement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One restart per live chat whose launch-time canvas mode differs from current configuration, paid on that chat's next turn or idle canvas open. Once relaunched, the stored wrapper flag matches and later operations do not restart for this reason.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh and replacement are serialized by each chat's queue. A setting change does not eagerly fan out across sessions; separate chats restart only as users next operate them.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The launch-time mode is retained on CopilotSessionWrapper and compared to current root configuration. Matching warm sessions take no restart. Cold sessions launch directly with current configuration. The state transition acts as a one-shot invalidation until replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new reason is directly in the refresh decision and replacement path, with per-chat queueing and wrapper state proving one-shot behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime resume latency and the number of simultaneously warm chats vary, but no bulk restart is scheduled and ordinary no-change turns add only a constant in-memory comparison.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The restart is a bounded, deferred configuration transition required for correct runtime capabilities; it is not repeated after replacement and does not eagerly fan out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Retrying a pinned-canvas reopen after extension consent was declined
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The notification action sends one retryDeniedConsent open and then shows/reconnects the pin. If membership has not propagated when show runs, the reconnect path can issue another stable-instance open; publication may otherwise bind immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry renderer-to-Agent Host openSessionCanvas with extension-consent retry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One explicit retry IPC; potentially one additional stable-instance IPC if publication lags behind the response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pinned canvases had no consent-aware reopen or retry path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first retry is required to relaunch/authorize the extension; a possible follow-up occurs while waiting for membership.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: SDK rpc.canvas.open for the retried stable instance
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one; at most two sequential calls in the response-before-publication edge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No pinned-canvas retry invoked the SDK open boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider authorization/activation and opening must complete before the pin can become live.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Consent retry is per explicitly clicked notification action for one pin. The normal reopen remains coalesced; the edge can produce at most two sequential stable-instance opens for that action, with total pins capped at five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The retry open is awaited before show. A possible follow-up is sequential for that pin, not a burst; different user actions/pins can overlap but require separate interaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: If the first retry publishes membership before resolving, show binds from warm membership and sends no follow-up. If response precedes publication, stable instance identity lets the runtime focus/reuse the same canvas on a follow-up. Declined state is not automatically retried.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Medium-high for the possible second call, lower for concrete performance impact because runtime deduplication cost is not evidenced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository explicitly supports response-before-publication, but the cost of a second stable-instance open after the first succeeds is not established; it may be an inexpensive idempotent focus. The trigger also requires a prior denial plus an explicit retry.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Although a narrow sequential duplicate call is possible when publication lags, the trigger is rare, bounded, user-driven, and the diff does not establish a concrete user-visible performance degradation from the idempotent second open.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and traced pinned-canvas restoration, consent retry, Agent Host IPC/runtime launch, and next-turn configuration refresh. The added expensive work is user-triggered or one-shot, bounded by five pins and per-chat sequencing, and replaces previously failed behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
